guard: an error terminal owed to the open run is published in place of the first finish the mapper produces for that run, and any terminal for that run settles the debt
why: A turn that failed while its terminal could not be written is owed an error terminal. When the
plane comes back with the next prompt already among the unread records, that prompt's mapping
closes the failed run as a finish; the emitter must publish the owed error in that finish's
place, or the failed turn is recorded as finished (Sol, round 5 of PR 3836, through the built MCP
entry point). O1 publishes the synthesized finish as mapped. O2 leaves the debt standing after a
close settles the run, so the next debt is refused as a second one.

mutations.name: O1 the owed terminal is never applied: the synthesized finish is published as mapped
mutations.find:
const owed = this.owed;
    if (!owed) return events;
mutations.replace:
const owed = this.owed;
    if (!owed || owed) return events;
mutations.note: The round-5 defect as the wire saw it: one RUN_FINISHED for the failed run and no RUN_ERROR.

mutations.name: O2 a close does not settle the debt
mutations.note: A debt that outlives its run would be refused as a second debt on the next failed turn, or applied to a finish of a run it was never owed to.
